kakheti.name: Kakheti
kakheti.summary: Georgia's main wine region combines warm valley floors, Caucasus influence and a deep qvevri tradition.

saperavi.expect: Deeply colored and structured, with dark fruit, high acidity and firm tannin.

rkatsiteli.expect: High-acid and savory, ranging from crisp white styles to structured amber qvevri wines.

identity.setting: Warm continental valley with mountain influence

why.cause: Warm days and cooler mountain-influenced nights
why.effect: Support full ripening while retaining useful acidity.

why.cause: Traditional qvevri fermentation for some wines
why.effect: Can add texture, tannin and savory complexity, especially in skin-contact whites.

santorini.name: Santorini
santorini.summary: Wind, drought and volcanic soils shape intensely fresh Assyrtiko despite the island's heat.

assyrtiko.expect: Bone-dry, powerful and piercingly fresh, with citrus, saline and stony character.

why.effect: Keeps wines vivid even in a hot, dry climate.
Favor low yields and concentrated fruit while traditional vine training protects grapes.

naoussa.name: Naoussa
naoussa.summary: Naoussa is the classic home of Xinomavro: pale, high-acid, tannic and famously savory.

xinomavro.expect: High-acid and tannic with sour cherry, tomato-leaf and savory complexity.

influences: Cooler nights than southern Greek regions

why.cause: Xinomavro's naturally high tannin and acidity
why.effect: Creates a firm structure that can reward long ageing.
Help preserve perfume and red-fruit freshness.

tokaj.name: Tokaj
tokaj.summary: Furmint combines fierce acidity with orchard fruit and can range from dry mineral wines to legendary sweet styles.

furmint.decant: No decant for young dry styles
furmint.expect: Taut and high-acid with apple, quince and mineral detail; sweetness varies widely by style.

influences: Autumn humidity near the Bodrog and Tisza rivers

why.effect: Supports both dry wines and intensely sweet wines without losing freshness.
Can favor noble rot in suitable years for sweet styles.

douro.name: Douro
douro.summary: Steep schist terraces and intense heat create concentrated reds from native Portuguese varieties.

touriga-nacional.expect: Dense, floral and structured, with dark fruit, violet and firm tannin.

why.effect: Promote deep ripeness and concentration in thick-skinned red grapes.
Often produce small crops with substantial flavor concentration.

canelones.name: Canelones
canelones.summary: Uruguay's signature Tannat combines Atlantic freshness with dark fruit and substantial structure.

tannat.expect: Dark, structured and fresh, with firm tannin, black fruit and savory detail.

influences: Atlantic and Río de la Plata influence

why.effect: Helps Tannat retain acidity alongside ripe dark fruit.
Often makes the traditionally tannic grape more polished and approachable.

vayots-dzor.name: Vayots Dzor
vayots-dzor.summary: High-elevation vineyards produce fragrant, fresh Areni Noir with red fruit and savory spice.

areni-noir.expect: Medium-bodied and aromatic, with bright red fruit, fresh acidity and herbal spice.

why.effect: Help preserve acidity and aromatic lift despite strong sunlight.
Reduce disease pressure and support concentrated small berries.

dealu-mare.name: Dealu Mare
dealu-mare.summary: Sunny southern slopes are one of Romania's leading red-wine zones and an important home for Fetească Neagră.

feteasca-neagra.expect: Ripe and spicy with dark fruit, moderate-firm tannin and savory depth.

identity.terrain: Long band of south-facing sub-Carpathian hills

why.effect: Support reliable ripening for structured red varieties.

why.cause: Cooler nights near the Carpathian foothills
why.effect: Help retain freshness and aromatic detail.

tenerife.name: Tenerife / Canary Islands
tenerife.summary: Volcanic island vineyards and altitude give Listán Negro a light, smoky and peppery personality.

listan-negro.expect: Light to medium-bodied, peppery and smoky, with fresh red fruit and bright acidity.

identity.terrain: Volcanic slopes rising from the Atlantic
identity.soil: Young volcanic ash and basaltic material
influences: Phylloxera-free old vines in many sites

why.effect: Temper subtropical warmth and help retain freshness.

why.cause: Low-input old-vine sites on volcanic terrain
why.effect: Often yield distinctive, savory wines with relatively modest body.
